stem: In a school garden in Jaipur, Meera observes that the roots of a neem sapling absorb water from the soil. Which type of habitat interaction is this?

options.text: biotic–biotic interaction, because both the neem and the water are needed for growth
biotic–abiotic interaction, because a living plant interacts with non-living water
abiotic–abiotic interaction, because water and soil are both non-living
no interaction, because the soil and water never meet the plant directly

teacher.key_rationale: A plant (living/biotic component) absorbing water (non-living/abiotic component) is a biotic–abiotic interaction, so B is correct. Option A is the trap for a student who assumes any interaction helping a living thing must be biotic–biotic; C mistakes the surrounding materials rather than the actual interacting pair; D denies a real interaction.
